history.question: In what year did World War II end?
history.explanation: WWII ended in 1945 when Japan surrendered after the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

history.question: Who was the first President of the United States?
history.hint: He is known as the 'Father of His Country'.
history.explanation: George Washington served as the first U.S. President from 1789 to 1797.

history.question: Which ancient civilization built the pyramids of Giza?
history.hint: This civilization thrived along the Nile River.
history.explanation: The ancient Egyptians built the pyramids of Giza around 2580-2560 BC as tombs for their pharaohs.

history.question: Which of the following were causes of World War I? (Select all that apply)
options: a) Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
c) Rise of nationalism in Europe
d) Alliance system among European powers
history.hint: The war started in 1914, well before the stock market crash.
history.explanation: WWI was caused by a combination of the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, rampant nationalism, and a web of mutual defense alliances. The Great Depression happened in 1929, after the war.

history.question: What empire did Julius Caesar lead?
history.explanation: Julius Caesar was a Roman general and statesman who played a critical role in the events leading to the downfall of the Roman Republic and the rise of the Roman Empire.

history.question: The Berlin Wall fell in which year?
history.hint: It happened near the end of the Cold War.
history.explanation: The Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989, marking a pivotal moment in the end of the Cold War and leading to German reunification in 1990.

science.question: What is the chemical symbol for water?
science.explanation: Water is composed of 2 hydrogen atoms and 1 oxygen atom, giving it the formula H2O.

science.question: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
science.hint: It is the fourth planet from the Sun.
science.explanation: Mars appears red due to iron oxide (rust) on its surface.

science.question: Which of the following are noble gases? (Select all that apply)
science.hint: Noble gases are in the last column of the periodic table.
science.explanation: Helium, Neon, and Argon are all noble gases. Oxygen is a reactive nonmetal.

science.question: What force keeps planets in orbit around the Sun?
science.explanation: Gravity is the attractive force between masses. The Sun's immense gravity keeps planets in elliptical orbits around it.

science.question: Which of these are parts of the human cell? (Select all that apply)
science.hint: One of these is found only in plant cells.
science.explanation: Human (animal) cells contain a nucleus, mitochondria, and cell membrane. Chloroplasts are found only in plant cells for photosynthesis.

science.question: What is the speed of light in a vacuum (approximately)?
science.explanation: The speed of light in a vacuum is approximately 299,792 km/s, commonly rounded to 300,000 km/s.

music.question: Which artist released the album 'Thriller'?
music.hint: He was known as the 'King of Pop'.
music.explanation: Michael Jackson released 'Thriller' in 1982. It became the best-selling album of all time.

music.question: Which of these instruments are in a standard string quartet? (Select all that apply)
music.hint: All the correct answers are string instruments.
music.explanation: A string quartet consists of 2 violins, 1 viola, and 1 cello. A flute is a woodwind instrument.

music.question: What genre of music originated in New Orleans in the early 20th century?
music.hint: Louis Armstrong is one of its most famous pioneers.
music.explanation: Jazz originated in New Orleans in the late 19th/early 20th century, blending African-American musical traditions.

music.question: Which band was Freddie Mercury the lead singer of?
music.explanation: Freddie Mercury was the lead vocalist of Queen, a British rock band formed in 1970 known for theatrical performances and diverse musical styles.

music.question: Which of these artists have won Grammy Award for Album of the Year more than once? (Select all that apply)
music.hint: Think about record-breaking artists in the modern and classic eras.
music.explanation: Taylor Swift has won Album of the Year four times (a record), and Stevie Wonder won three times. Frank Sinatra and Beyonce have not won Album of the Year.

music.question: The 'Rite of Spring' was composed by which composer?
music.hint: Its 1913 premiere caused a riot in the audience.
music.explanation: Igor Stravinsky composed 'The Rite of Spring' for the Ballets Russes. Its dissonant harmonies and irregular rhythms caused a famous riot at its Paris premiere in 1913.

nba.question: Which player has won the most NBA championship rings?
nba.hint: He played for the Boston Celtics in the 1950s and 60s.
nba.explanation: Bill Russell won 11 NBA championships with the Boston Celtics between 1957 and 1969.

nba.question: Which team has won the most NBA championships?
nba.hint: This team is based in Massachusetts.
nba.explanation: The Boston Celtics have won 18 NBA championships, the most in league history.

nba.question: Which of these players were selected first overall in the NBA Draft? (Select all that apply)
nba.hint: One of the wrong answers was drafted 13th overall.
nba.explanation: LeBron James (2003), Tim Duncan (1997), and Anthony Edwards (2020) were all #1 picks. Kobe Bryant was picked 13th in 1996.

nba.question: Who holds the NBA record for most career points scored?
nba.hint: He surpassed the previous record in 2023.
nba.explanation: LeBron James surpassed Kareem Abdul-Jabbar's long-standing record of 38,387 points in February 2023, becoming the all-time NBA scoring leader.

nba.question: Which of these players won back-to-back NBA Finals MVP awards? (Select all that apply)
nba.hint: Both won it with the same team in consecutive years.
nba.explanation: Michael Jordan won Finals MVP in 1991-1993 and 1996-1998. Shaquille O'Neal won it in 2000, 2001, and 2002 with the Lakers. LeBron and Magic each won it only once in non-consecutive years.

nba.question: What year was the NBA founded?
nba.hint: It happened shortly after World War II ended.
nba.explanation: The Basketball Association of America (BAA), which later became the NBA, was founded on June 6, 1946.

geography.question: What is the capital of Australia?
geography.hint: It is not the largest city in Australia.
geography.explanation: Canberra is Australia's capital. It was purpose-built to resolve a rivalry between Sydney and Melbourne over which city should be the capital.

geography.question: Which of these countries share a land border with France? (Select all that apply)
geography.hint: One of these is separated from France by the English Channel.
geography.explanation: France shares land borders with Spain, Italy, Germany, Switzerland, Belgium, Luxembourg, and Monaco. The United Kingdom is separated from France by the English Channel.

geography.question: What is the longest river in the world?
geography.explanation: The Nile River, flowing through northeastern Africa, is generally considered the world's longest river at approximately 6,650 km.

geography.question: Which continent has the most countries?
geography.explanation: Africa has the most countries of any continent, with 54 recognized sovereign nations.

geography.question: Mount Everest is located on the border of which two countries?
geography.hint: It is in the Himalayas, between South Asia and East Asia.
geography.explanation: Mount Everest sits on the border between Nepal and China (Tibet). The peak was first summited by Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay in 1953.

geography.question: Which of these are island nations? (Select all that apply)
geography.hint: One of the answers is on the Iberian Peninsula.
geography.explanation: Japan, Iceland, and New Zealand are all island nations entirely surrounded by ocean. Portugal is located on the Iberian Peninsula and shares a land border with Spain.
